title: Metrics ingestion: buffer the firehose, roll up the reads
brief: Design a Datadog-style metrics backend. Agents send batches of points (one request = one batch); dashboards query them. Points end up in a time-series store (a Wide-column block, 10k ops/s per replica).

requirements: intake must keep accepting while the store is down (the twist checks it)
variants.twist: The store is down for 30 s: kill_node on it, then restore_node. Intake should stay green while the backlog builds, then drain. Does yours?

requirements: 20k rps, 30% dashboard queries: there's an incident and everyone opens dashboards
Each query reads about 20 series: mark the read edge into the store as fan-out read (the lesson sets following = 20)
variants.twist: A customer adds a user_id tag: 10x the series per query. Apply with set_traffic(following=200). Raw points or pre-aggregated rollups? What does high cardinality cost in storage?

hints: If the store slows down or dies, what happens to an agent sending points right now?
Put a log (a stream) between intake and the store, with aggregator consumers writing in the background; one consumer per partition reads. For dashboards: does every query have to read 20 raw series?

Ingest: intake writes into a log, and consumers move the data into the store; match consumers to partitions. Incident: dashboards shouldn't each read 20 raw series. What could hold pre-computed answers, and where does the fan-out read edge go then?
_notes: Intake 25 services (rho 0.8, $2.50) + LB. Writing straight to wide-column (3 x 10k) passes steady (p99 ~35 ms, $3.73) but a store kill fails 100% of requests. Kafka ($0.63, 10k/partition) -> aggregator services (1k/s each) -> store: 24 partitions + 24 consumers: p99 ~38 ms, $6.76, and a store kill leaves intake green: batches pile up as lag (and get redelivered), then drain after the restore. 4 partitions with 24 consumers: only 4 read, backlog explodes. Incident (fan-out 20 on reads): no cache needs ~14-16 store replicas ($10-11). Cache 0.9 with the fan-out edge after it: store rho 0.87 on 3 replicas, p99 ~40 ms, $6.11. Aggregation that shrinks write volume isn't modeled; consumers forward every batch. Discuss rollups, downsampling and cardinality limits. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
